turns.text: I need some advice on what to do next. It has been three days of complete silence from Julian since that text I sent on Tuesday, and every time I sit down to draft a follow-up, I just hit a wall. I'm definitely not sending another message over the weekend, so what is the actual move here?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text:
The actual move is nothing until Monday, and then it's not a follow-up message. You already said what needed saying in that text — it was honest, didn't demand a reply, and left the door open. Three days of silence on his side doesn't mean it landed badly; it means he's sitting with it, or doesn't know what to say yet, or needs space.

A second message this soon would pressure the silence instead of respecting it. Let Monday come. If you still want to reach out, make it a low-stakes reason to be in the same room — desk cover, a question about a Foothill account, something that puts you both at the counter without having to address the Tuesday text. The conversation picks up from presence, not from another drafted apology.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The recommendation was clear right in the first sentence, but stacking so many background points and extra caveats behind it was a lot to wade through when the answer was already there.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Got it. Nothing until Monday, then a low-stakes reason to be at the desk together — not another message.
